items.note: Read the signed PDF (2 pages, German/Italian). Order 127/2026 of the traffic assessor (Lukas Luggin), dated 27 July 2026: parking in the marked spaces north of the Mendelbahn valley station in St. Anton (plots 6886/10 and 6886/15) limited to 180 minutes with parking disc, 'Werk- sowie Feiertags' (weekdays and holidays, i.e. every day) 08:30-19:00; disc with arrival time must be displayed; reference to the STA/municipality agreement on managing the outdoor area (prot. 0040063/2026); purpose is adequate turn-over; enters into force after vertical and horizontal signs are installed. Every claim in the draft matches. Whether the signs are installed yet is not stated, and the draft correctly words it as taking effect once installed.

Page published 21.08.2026 (last updated 14.09.2026), signed by mayor Christoph Pillon. It says the Lido lease ('Lido-Pachtzins') and the car park are important income, lake access is free mornings and evenings, he says no to an ill-considered free lake access on the north shore, asks 'Wo wird geparkt?' among other questions, and that after the positive first-instance ruling for the municipality the free-access case is before the Council of State (Staatsrat). All of it is the mayor's own opinion and the draft attributes it as such.

Interview in Alto Adige, 13 June 2025, by Massimiliano Bona. Correct: Anderlan (26, SVP) was given a mandate by the mayor for lake matters; Lido guests (municipal Lido or the private Gretl) do not pay parking in addition; the former military area lacks water, electricity and parking (also near a Natura 2000 biotope). Not supported: the draft says the first sketch was 'for improving the existing public access'. In the interview the sketch is the answer to 'Nessuna proposta concreta del Comune?', right after the discussion of a nature trail at the military area, and it is not tied to the existing access. He also says separately that the municipality is working on a project to make the current site more attractive.
items.corrected_text: In June 2025 the SVP councillor Anton Anderlan, who had been given responsibility for lake matters by the mayor, said in an interview that visitors to the municipal Lido do not pay parking on top of entry, and that the former military site on the lake is unsuitable because it lacks water, electricity and parking. Asked whether the municipality had a concrete proposal, he said its surveyor had drawn up only a first sketch. He also said the municipality was working on a project to make the existing lake access more attractive.

items.note: Municipal news item published 28.08.2026 (last updated 22.09.2026): the traffic rules of the kindergarten and school street apply again from the start of school on 7 September 2026; the section from Rottenburgerplatz towards Maria-Theresien-Straße is traffic-calmed 07:15-08:15 and 12:40-13:10. Matches. Little direct parking relevance.

Alto Adige, 24 January 2016 (Massimiliano Bona): the town executive decided in its last session to raise all car park tariffs; last increase 13 May 2013. Listed per hour: village centre 1.50 to 1.60; near village (Rottenburg square, Soelva, Station Street) 1 to 1.10; peripheral 0.50 to 0.60; Trucci 0.80 to 0.90; Lido 0.80 to 1 euro with a 5 euro daily maximum. All numbers match. This is a newspaper report, not a listing portal. The figures are ten years old and the draft says so, which is the right wording. Current tariffs are not shown.

Alto Adige, 5 May 2012: parking at the lake is paid again from that week; blue municipal spaces or spaces with a daily rate (up to 5 euros) or hourly rate of the various facilities on the lake; Lido visitors exempt if they give their plate number at the cash desk; shuttle bus from 1 May to October. The page does not say the facilities are 'private car parks'; it says 'varie strutture che si affacciano sul bacino lacustre'. Rest matches. Very old figure.
items.corrected_text: In May 2012 the municipal police announced that parking at the lake was paid again from that week: blue-zone municipal spaces, or spaces of the various facilities on the lake with a daily rate (up to 5 euros) or an hourly rate. Lido visitors were exempt if they gave their plate number at the cash desk, and a shuttle bus to the lake ran from 1 May to October that year. This is a 2012 report and not a current tariff.

items.note: suedtirol.live is a commercial listing portal ('Become a partner & get a free listing', operated by First Avenue GmbH, 'No business hours known'), not an official or primary source. The page does say 1.20 euro/hour, daily 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., and exemption for Lido restaurant/pool guests after plate registration at the terminal, but it is undated, unattributed and conflicts with the 2016 figure of 1 euro. Not acceptable for a tariff fact.

Page of the South Tyrol tourism portal (undated). Confirms: large paid car park in front of the Lido; 'auch der Bus Nr. 138 hält am See'; three evenings in July and August are dedicated to music, the Kalterer Seespiele on the lake stage. The season line reads 'Die Saison ... ist beendet, die Badesaison 2027 beginnt Mitte Mai', so it speaks about the 2027 season, not 'usually'. The word 'concerts' is also an inference. Bus number 138 conflicts with line 130 on the suedtirol.info page (item 9) and cannot be resolved from these pages.
items.corrected_text: The South Tyrol tourism page for the Lido Kalterer See (read 21 October 2026, undated) describes a large paid car park in front of the Lido and says bus line 138 stops at the lake. It says three evenings in July and August are dedicated to music with the Kalterer Seespiele on the lake stage, and that the 2027 bathing season begins in mid-May.

items.note: Page (read 21 October 2026, shows opening times from 21 Oct): 'Seit 2021 wird die Mendelbahn von der Südtiroler Transportstrukturen AG (STA) gefuehrt'; autumn timetable 15.09.2026-09.11.2026 daily 08:30-20:00; 13.50 euro return (8.50 single); bus line Bozen-Kaltern (no. 132) stops there; replacement bus B134 from Rottenburger Platz during the yearly spring and autumn maintenance weeks. All claims match.

Page of the South Tyrol tourism portal (IDM, undated) says: board bus line 130 in Kaltern and get off after 5 minutes at the centre of the lake; from Bozen the Überetsch Express (line 131) reaches Kaltern in 30 minutes at a quarter-hour frequency. Claims match, but they sit on an undated marketing page and the Lido page of the same portal names line 138 for the lake. The draft's remark that line numbers should be checked is an editing note, not publishable text. Corrected text states the conflict neutrally.
items.corrected_text: The South Tyrol tourism site (read 21 October 2026, undated) says bus line 130 takes about 5 minutes from Kaltern to the centre of the lake, and that the Überetsch Express (line 131) runs from Bozen to Kaltern in 30 minutes at a quarter-hour frequency. The same portal's Lido page names line 138 for the lake, so the line numbers in these tourism sources are inconsistent.

items.note: suedtirol.live is a commercial listing portal (free partner listings, 'Derzeit leider keine bekannt' opening hours, undated). The entry text does list Alperia charging stations at Parkplatz Weinstrasse (P5), the Mendelbahn valley station, the Lido and the primary school in Oberplanitzing, payable via the Neogy app or credit card/PayPal, but a listing portal is not acceptable for this fact and the number of charging points and availability are not given.

Südtirol News, published 2024-09-11, 'Heute' signed in Bozen by the governor, the mayor (Benin Bernard) and the winery chairman: the agreement enables the urban restructuring of the winery and station area and a Park & Ride car park for commuters and passengers of the Überetsch bus services, free for Südtirol Pass holders ('kann ein Parkhaus gebaut werden'). The bus parking behind the station moves to Kaltern Gand with e-charging for buses; a provisional bus area is set up on the winery site until completion. Matches. Note the mayor then was Gertrud Benin Bernard, not the current mayor.

SALTO, 12 Sept 2024 (updated 12.9.2024, 21:43): construction costs for the car park about 3.8 million euros, financed by municipality and province; the replacement bus park at Kaltern Gand about 4.2 million euros, still in the planning phase, implementation 'stockt' (stalls); update says the municipal council dealt with and approved the project by majority on 12 Sept; opposition councillor Oberparleiter (Dorfliste) criticised it (before the vote). No number of spaces is given. The planning start was announced for 2024 by the provincial councillor; no building schedule is given. Matches the draft.

Municipal news published 02.10.2026 (updated 20.10.2026): ground-breaking for the retail lot ('Baulos Handel') in the winery area; the new supermarket is at the village entrance; a new residential area is planned; the renovation of the former station area a few metres to the south is prepared. The agreement of province, municipality and winery is said to cover housing, retail and mobility zones, but the release says nothing about the car park or its schedule. Matches.

Municipal 'Mobilität' page (undated). Confirms: 'Klimafreundliche Mobilität in Kaltern' started at the end of 2021, with a mobility survey and a mobility concept among its actions; eBike charging stations under the cycling project; a car-free cycling day to the Mendel organised every year since 2007; no parking measures. Not on the page: 'over 300 participants' in the survey (no participant number appears).
items.corrected_text: The municipal mobility page (read 21 October 2026, undated) describes the 'Klimafreundliche Mobilität in Kaltern' project started at the end of 2021, with actions including a mobility survey and a mobility concept, and a cycling project that includes e-bike charging stations. It notes a car-free cycling day to the Mendel organised every year since 2007. No parking measures are listed there.

corrected_summary: Caldaro (Kaltern an der Weinstraße, about 8,200 inhabitants) issued municipal order 127/2026 on 27 July 2026, which limits parking at the marked spaces north of the Mendelbahn valley station in St. Anton to 180 minutes with a parking disc, 08:30 to 19:00 every day, taking effect once signs are installed; the funicular itself is run by the provincial company STA. In a column of 21 August 2026 the mayor wrote that the Lido lease and the Lido car park are important income for the municipality, that lake access is free in the morning and evening, and that the free-access court case is before the Council of State; he argued against a hastily decided free access on the north shore and asked where cars would park. The main development project is a Park & Ride car park in the winery and station area, agreed between province, municipality and winery on 11 September 2024 and reported by SALTO at about 3.8 million euros, free for Südtirol Pass holders; the bus parking is to move to Kaltern Gand, and the supermarket part of the area broke ground in October 2026, but no building schedule for the car park was found. The only tariff figures found on a readable newspaper page are from 2016 (Lido 1 euro per hour with a 5 euro daily maximum) and are ten years old; current official tariffs, EV charging details and lake traffic figures could not be confirmed from primary sources, and tourism sources disagree on the bus line number for the lake (130 or 138).
